 Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson will start Wednesday’s game against the Kings. 
 Dunn is good to go after missing most of the preseason with a minor injury, and he’ll start alongside Garland in the backcourt. Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue said on Saturday that Jackson would start at center, so his inclusion is unsurprising. Garland and Hachimura should lead the starters offensively. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Source:  Tomer Azarly

 Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue said Saturday that Isaiah Jackson will begin the regular season as the team’s starting center. 
 Jackson was the starter throughout the preseason, so Saturday’s news is not a complete surprise. However, the confirmation makes him an even better option for fantasy managers who need a center in the later rounds of their drafts. Brook Lopez will be the backup, and that limits his fantasy value considerably. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson accounted for nine points (4-of-8 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Nuggets. 
 Wednesday’s game was the Clippers’ last preseason game, so it’s fair to question how much of a “dress rehearsal” it was for Tyronn Lue’s team. Jackson started again and played 26 minutes, while veteran Brook Lopez (nine points, two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer) logged eight minutes off the bench. If Jackson can lock down the starting job, his upside would make him worthy of late-round consideration in drafts. And even if he doesn’t start, the Clippers will be light on centers until Yanic Konan Niederhäuser is cleared to return from the foot injury that ended his 2025-26 season in March. 
 Jordan Miller 
 LAC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Jordan Miller underwent surgery on a torn left rotator cuff and will be reevaluated in six months. 
 Miller’s injury could mean additional run for Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn, though the pair will compete with Gradey Dick, Bradley Beal and Darius Garland for minutes. 
 Max Strus 
 LAC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Max Strus has been traded to the Clippers as part of the three-team deal that sent Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers. 
 Strus will get a fresh start after three seasons in Cleveland. His defense and floor spacing should help make an immediate impact for the Clippers as they look to establish a new identity in the post-Kawhi Leonard era. Strus could start alongside Darius Garland, but his presence in a crowded backcourt will make the rotation difficult to project. Kris Dunn, Bennedict Mathurin (RFA) and Gradey Dick all stand to lose out on minutes with Strus on the squad. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson (ankle) is available to play against the Warriors on Wednesday. 
 Jackson will be good to go, making this his first appearance since March 27. He has typically filled out the backup center minutes behind Brook Lopez, but in an elimination game, the rotations could look different, especially since it has been nearly three weeks since Jackson last suited up. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson (ankle) has been upgraded to probable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Jackson has been sidelined since March 27, but after practicing fully on Tuesday, he is now expected to make his return for the Clippers’ win-or-go-home matchup with the Warriors. He’ll likely occupy some of the backup center minutes behind Brook Lopez. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson (ankle) fully participated in Tuesday’s practice, including 5-on-5. 
 Jackson has been out since spraining his ankle during a March 27 win over the Pacers, leaving the Clippers without a legitimate backup center. John Collins has filled the void in Jackson’s absence and would continue to do so if he can’t return for Wednesday’s Play-In Tournament game against the Warriors. 
 John Collins 
 LAC 
 Forward-Center 
 #20 
 John Collins accounted for 18 points (8-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs) and nine rebounds in Sunday’s win over the Warriors. 
 With no Kawhi Leonard (ankle), Collins returned to the Clippers’ starting lineup after coming off the bench in three of the previous four games. He finished one rebound shy of a double-double against the Warriors, but Collins produced nothing else in his 21 minutes on the floor. Leonard will be available for Wednesday’s rematch with the Warriors, which would relegate Collins to the backup center role he’s been asked to assume since Isaiah Jackson went down. 
 Isaiah Jackson 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Isaiah Jackson (ankle) is out for Sunday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Jackson has been out since March 27, and he will remain out for Sunday’s season finale. John Collins has served as the backup center, a role that eventually prompted Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue to move him to the bench. With Kawhi Leonard (ankle) questionable, Collins’ opportunities may increase on Sunday. 
 John Collins 
 LAC 
 Forward-Center 
 #20 
 John Collins will replace Darius Garland (foot) in the starting lineup for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Wednesday’s game is the second in as many nights for the Clippers, who beat the Mavericks on Tuesday. As a result, Garland will sit for injury management reasons, with Collins moving into the starting lineup. Kris Dunn will run the point, which raises his fantasy ceiling.

 LaMelo Ball recorded 21 points (7-of-17 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, six assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Heat.
 Ball looked comfortable with his new team, pairing with Anthony Edwards to hit 14-of-30 from the arc. Just as big for fantasy managers, especially those in category leagues, was Ball’s single turnover in 28 minutes. Expecting him to do that consistently would be greedy, but Minnesota’s lineup should keep Ball from feeling like he has to do too much offensively. Which would be great for his fantasy outlook. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Tyrese Haliburton

 Tyrese Haliburton had 23 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, 12 assists, one steal and two three-pointers in the Pacers’ 123-120 victory over the Pelicans on Wednesday. 
 Haliburton was overcome with emotion in the postgame interview after he had 23 points and the Pacers won the first game he’s played since he suffered a torn Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. It was certainly a meaningful milestone for the 26-year-old point guard, who was also diagnosed with shingles while recovering from his torn Achilles. Haliburton was sharp in the preseason and in the regular season opener he looked ready to deliver first-round fantasy value once again. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Anthony Edwards finished Wednesday’s win over the Heat with 45 points (16-of-29 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and nine three-pointers.
 Despite all the attention on Giannis Antetokounmpo’s official Heat debut, Edwards stole the show on Wednesday. The Timberwolves’ star guard scored at least nine points in each quarter, including 15 in the third. Edwards and LaMelo Ball became the first Timberwolves tandem to hit at least five three-pointers in the same season opener. Also, he’s the first player in franchise history to score 30 or more in consecutive openers. This was a great start for Edwards and those who have him rostered. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Keyonte George with 22 points (7-of-12 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, and four 3-pointers in Wednesday’s season debut.
 Keyonte George continued right where he left off last season and continued to get buckets. He will need to do more than score if he’s going to help lead the Jazz to the playoffs. He will likely continue to put up numbers throughout the year.

 Matas Buzelis accounted for 17 points (2-of-7 FGs, 13-of-16 FTs), six rebounds and two blocks in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors.
 As a team, the Bulls shot 31.8 percent from the field on Wednesday, so Buzelis wasn’t the only one to have an off night. The good news for fantasy managers was that he got to the foul line often, which boosted his point total. Toronto isn’t an easy matchup for wings, so the hope is that Buzelis will bounce back on Friday in Milwaukee.

 Darryn Peterson puts up 9 points (3-of-7 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, and three assists in NBA debut.
 It was a difficult night all around for the Jazz. Obviously, we would want him to be more aggressive, but it was his first real NBA game. He’ll be much better than this. I like the fact that he was second on the team in minutes, which shows the trust Will Hardy has in him. If you have him, be patient, but he was going later in redraft leagues anyway, so if he doesn’t start producing soon, you can feel free to move on.

 Josh Giddey produced two points (1-of-10 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds and six assists in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors.
 None of the Bulls played particularly well in Wednesday’s 135-92 defeat, so this result can’t be pinned on Giddey alone. The concern for fantasy managers is that his cold shooting in the preseason carried over into Wednesday’s season opener. The hope is that Giddey will bounce back on Friday when the Bulls visit the Bucks, who are also rebuilding.

 Michael Porter Jr. had 26 points (10-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist, three steals and five three-pointers against the Hornets on Wednesday. 
 Porter averaged 1.1 steals last year, which was his career-high. He was active on defense Wednesday, recording three steals in the process. Porter poured in points on the offensive end as well, finishing with 26 points and five three-pointers. In his first game playing with Julius Randle, Porter showed that he can coexist with another high-level teammate. The two combined for 59 points in the first game of what should be a productive partnership. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Caleb Wilson notched 16 points (7-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Raptors.
 Regardless of position, efficiency can be an issue for rookies, and that was certainly the case for Wilson in his official NBA debut. In addition to shooting 33.3 percent from the field, the lottery pick out of North Carolina racked up nine turnovers. Wilson will be a high-usage player this season, but that may hurt his fantasy value, especially for those who can’t afford a major drop in field-goal percentage or an increase in turnovers. The good news is that the rookie has better nights ahead, because Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard are challenging matchups for any wing. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaren Jackson didn’t have the best game on his first return to Memphis. He got into fouled out, and the Grizzlies were not scared of him on the court. He had 5 turnovers, which hurts that category for managers. While the stat line is not amazing, he wasn’t that good on the court. They took advantage of the lack of physicality relentlessly in this game.
